title: Reading an Enum Back
goal: match tells you which variant you have, and hands you its data.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 2 Morning: Pattern Matching

sections.text: You met `match` in the Control Flow deck, where it compared a plain value against a list of options. On an enum it does one more thing. It also hands you the data the variant is carrying.

sections.caption: n and s are the data, pulled out of the variant.

sections.text: The name inside the brackets is yours to choose. It binds to whatever that variant is carrying, and it only exists inside that arm.
The exhaustiveness rule now earns its keep. A `match` on an enum has to cover every variant, and the compiler counts them. Miss one and you get error `E0004` before the code ever runs.
That check is worth more than it looks. Add a variant to the enum six months from now, and every `match` that forgot about it becomes a compile error instead of a bug in production.
You can still write `_` as a catch-all, but on an enum it is usually the wrong choice. It silences exactly the error you want.
